guide.summary: Geometric optics models light as rays. This unit covers reflection and plane, concave, and convex mirrors; refraction, Snell's law, and total internal reflection; and thin lenses, including ray diagrams, the thin-lens/mirror equation, magnification, and image characteristics.

sections.heading: Reflection and mirrors
sections.body: Law of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, both measured from the normal. A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image the same size and the same distance behind the mirror. A concave (converging) mirror has a positive focal length f = R/2; it forms real, inverted images for objects beyond f and virtual, upright, magnified images for objects inside f. A convex (diverging) mirror has negative f and always forms virtual, upright, reduced images. Principal rays: parallel to the axis → through (or away from) the focal point; through the focal point → parallel; to the center of the mirror → reflects symmetrically.

sections.heading: Refraction
sections.body: Index of refraction n = c/v ≥ 1. Light changes speed and wavelength (not frequency) entering a new medium. Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; entering a higher-n medium, light bends toward the normal. Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from higher n to lower n at an angle greater than the critical angle, sin θ_c = n₂/n₁ (fiber optics). Dispersion: n varies slightly with wavelength, separating colors in a prism.

sections.heading: Thin lenses
sections.body: Converging (convex) lenses have positive f; diverging (concave) lenses have negative f. Thin-lens equation: 1/s_o + 1/s_i = 1/f. Magnification M = h_i/h_o = −s_i/s_o. Sign conventions: positive s_i means a real image (on the opposite side of a lens, the same side for a mirror), which is inverted (M < 0); negative s_i means a virtual image, upright (M > 0). For converging lenses: object beyond 2f → real, inverted, reduced; between f and 2f → real, inverted, enlarged; at f → no image; inside f → virtual, upright, enlarged (magnifier). Diverging lenses always form virtual, upright, reduced images. A lens's focal length depends on its shape and the index of refraction relative to the surrounding medium; submerging a glass lens in water increases its focal length.

keyTakeaways: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; toward normal in higher n.
TIR: from higher n to lower n beyond θ_c.
Real images inverted; virtual images upright.
Diverging lenses and convex mirrors: always virtual, upright, smaller.
commonMistakes: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
Sign errors with diverging lenses (f negative).
Saying TIR can occur when light enters a denser medium.
Forgetting that covering half a lens dims the image but doesn't remove half of it.
examTips: Draw at least two principal rays for every image question.
State real/virtual, upright/inverted, enlarged/reduced with reasons.
Snell's law questions often ask for a ratio of speeds or wavelengths.
Lab FRQs: plot 1/s_i vs. 1/s_o; intercept gives 1/f.
guide.cramSheet:
**Reflection:** θ_i = θ_r · plane mirror: virtual, upright, same size

**Mirrors:** concave f > 0 (R/2) · convex f < 0

**Refraction:** n = c/v · n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ · f unchanged, λ changes

**TIR:** n₁ > n₂ · sin θ_c = n₂/n₁

**Lenses:** 1/s_o + 1/s_i = 1/f · M = −s_i/s_o · converging f > 0, diverging f < 0

**Images:** s_i > 0 real inverted · s_i < 0 virtual upright

**Converging:** > 2f reduced · f to 2f enlarged · < f virtual magnified

vocab.definition: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal.
n = c/v, the ratio of light's speed in vacuum to its speed in a medium.
n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ for light crossing a boundary.
The angle of incidence beyond which total internal reflection occurs: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁.
Complete reflection of light at a boundary when going from higher to lower index beyond the critical angle.
Distance from a lens or mirror to the point where parallel rays converge (or appear to diverge).
An image formed where light rays actually converge; can be projected on a screen.
An image formed where rays appear to come from; cannot be projected.
A lens thicker in the middle that brings parallel rays to a focus; f > 0.
A lens thinner in the middle that spreads parallel rays; f < 0.
Separation of light into colors because n depends on wavelength.

practice.stem: The bottom half of a converging lens forming a real image on a screen is covered with black tape. What happens to the image?

choices.text: The bottom half of the image disappears.
The full image remains but is dimmer.
The top half of the image disappears.

practice.explanation: Every point of the object still sends rays through the uncovered half; less light reaches each image point.

practice.stem: Light passes from medium 1 into medium 2 and bends away from the normal. Which is true?

choices.text: n₁ > n₂, and light's wavelength increases in medium 2.
n₁ < n₂, and the wavelength decreases.

practice.explanation: Bending away from the normal means entering a lower-index (faster) medium; λ = v/f increases.

practice.stem: A glass converging lens (n = 1.5) has focal length 20 cm in air. When submerged in water (n = 1.33), its focal length

choices.text: increases, because the lens bends light less relative to water

practice.explanation: Refraction depends on the index difference between lens and surroundings; a smaller difference means weaker focusing.

distractors.A: Only if the surrounding index exceeded the lens's.

practice.stem: As an object moves from far away toward the focal point of a converging lens, the real image

choices.text: moves closer to the lens and gets smaller
moves farther from the lens and gets larger

practice.explanation: As s_o decreases toward f, s_i increases toward infinity and |M| = s_i/s_o grows.

practice.stem: An optical fiber has a glass core (n = 1.50) surrounded by cladding. To ensure total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary for the widest range of angles, the cladding should have

choices.text: a much lower index than the core
any index, because TIR always occurs

practice.explanation: Lower n₂ means smaller critical angle (sin θ_c = n₂/n₁), so more rays exceed it.

rubric.description: A ray parallel to the axis refracts through the far focal point; a ray through the center continues straight (or a ray through the near focal point exits parallel).
Rays intersect beyond 2f on the far side, below the axis (inverted, enlarged).
Virtual, upright, enlarged (3×), on the same side as the object.
Light rays only appear to diverge from the virtual image; they don't actually converge there, so no light reaches a screen at that location.

practice.sampleResponse:
A. A ray from the top of the object traveling parallel to the axis refracts through the focal point on the far side. A second ray through the center of the lens continues undeflected. These rays cross on the far side of the lens, farther than 24 cm away and below the axis, forming an inverted, enlarged image.

B. 1/s_o + 1/s_i = 1/f → 1/18 + 1/s_i = 1/12 → 1/s_i = 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36 → s_i = +36 cm.

C. M = −s_i/s_o = −36/18 = −2. h_i = M h_o = (−2)(2.0 cm) = −4.0 cm. The image is 4.0 cm tall and inverted.

D. 1/s_i = 1/12 − 1/8 = −1/24 → s_i = −24 cm. M = −(−24)/8 = +3. The image is virtual, upright, three times as tall as the object (6.0 cm), and located 24 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

E. The image is virtual: the refracted rays diverge after the lens and only appear to come from a point on the object's side. No light actually converges at the image location, so it cannot form on a screen.
